REFERRAL REASON
Evaluation for microsatellite instability in caecal adenocarcinoma

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Adult patient with caecal adenocarcinoma. Tissue submitted for microsatellite instability analysis as part of Lynch syndrome evaluation.

SPECIMEN
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) caecal adenocarcinoma tissue
Reference normal tissue from adjacent non-neoplastic colonic mucosa

METHODOLOGY
Microsatellite Instability (MSI) Analysis by PCR

DNA was extracted from both tumor and matched normal tissue using standard protocols. MSI analysis was performed using the GeneTech MSI Analysis System, which evaluates five quasi-monomorphic mononucleotide repeat markers:
- BAT-25
- BAT-26
- NR-21
- NR-24
- MONO-27

PCR amplification was performed using fluorescently labeled primers, and fragment analysis was conducted on an automated capillary electrophoresis system. The electropherograms from tumor and normal samples were compared to assess for instability at each marker.

RESULTS

Microsatellite Instability Status: MICROSATELLITE STABLE (MSS)

Marker Analysis:
BAT-25: Stable
BAT-26: Stable
NR-21: Stable
NR-24: Stable
MONO-27: Stable

All five microsatellite markers demonstrated stable patterns with no evidence of instability when comparing tumor to normal tissue.

INTERPRETATION
The tumor demonstrates microsatellite stability (MSS) with no evidence of microsatellite instability at any of the five markers tested. This result indicates no evidence of a mismatch repair gene defect in this tumor.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The MSS result is not suggestive of Lynch syndrome. Approximately 85% of colorectal carcinomas are microsatellite stable. The absence of MSI does not exclude the possibility of hereditary cancer syndromes caused by mechanisms other than mismatch repair deficiency.

EXPLANATORY NOTES
Microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is used to screen for defects in the DNA mismatch repair system. High-frequency MSI (MSI-H) is found in approximately 15% of colorectal carcinomas and is associated with Lynch syndrome in the hereditary setting or MLH1 promoter hypermethylation in the sporadic setting. The GeneTech MSI Analysis System has been validated to have >95% concordance with the Bethesda panel for MSI detection.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted name] Medical Center Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.
